title: Naan Bread
subtitle: Soft, pillowy Indian flatbread with charred bubbles
excerpt: A soft, slightly chewy leavened Indian flatbread, cooked in a blistering-hot pan to produce the characteristic charred spots and puffed bubbles of a tandoor-baked naan.

recipe.sourceNotes: Naan (or nan) is a leavened flatbread found across the South and Central Asian region, from India and Pakistan through Afghanistan, Iran, and the Central Asian republics. The word naan is derived from the Persian nan, simply meaning bread. In traditional Indian restaurants, naan is cooked by slapping the dough against the inner wall of a tandoor (cylindrical clay oven) that may reach temperatures of 480 C or higher. The bread cooks in 60 to 90 seconds with characteristic charring and large bubbles. In a domestic kitchen, a very hot cast-iron griddle or heavy frying pan replicates this effect reasonably well, though without the clay-oven smokiness. The dough uses yoghurt and baking powder in addition to yeast, which gives the characteristic slight tang and soft, slightly pillowy texture that distinguishes naan from plain flatbread. Garlic butter is the most popular serving addition in British Indian restaurants.

recipeTools.notes: A large, heavy cast-iron frying pan or griddle pan.

content.text: The pan must be as hot as it will go before the dough goes on: the intense initial heat is what creates the large bubbles and char marks. Do not add any oil to the pan. Wipe a dry cloth over the surface just before adding the dough. Cook the first side until the top surface is covered with large bubbles and the underside has dark charred spots, then flip and cook the second side briefly. Brush with melted garlic butter the moment the naan comes off the pan.

items.preparation: melted, with 2 cloves of garlic, for brushing
minced and cooked in the butter

content.text: Mix the flour, yeast, baking powder, sugar, and salt. Add the yoghurt, warm milk, and oil. Mix to a soft dough. Knead for 5 minutes until smooth. Place in an oiled bowl, cover, and leave for 1 hour until slightly puffed.
Divide into 6 balls. On a lightly floured surface, roll each to an oval about 5 mm thick and 20 cm long. Heat a large cast-iron pan over the highest heat possible for 5 minutes until very hot.

Cook each naan for 2 minutes until the top is covered with large bubbles and the underside has dark charred spots. Flip and cook for 1 minute. Remove and brush immediately with garlic butter. Keep warm in a folded cloth while cooking the rest. Serve within 15 minutes.
